title: Gilded Iznik dish
collectionTitle: Gilded Dish with Flowers and Leaves
fact: The catalogue lists a red slip, an underglaze design and overglaze gilding.
limit: The visible decoration does not establish which marks sit above the glaze. The catalogue names the order for this dish.
alt: Round dish with curved leaves and multicoloured bands.
material: Fritware with red slip, underglaze design, and overglaze gilding
dimensions: Diameter: 29.8 cm (11 3/4 in.); Overall: 6.6 cm (2 5/8 in.)

title: Iznik floral spandrel
fact: The catalogue records red slip and an underglaze design in fritware. Its missing right half would have completed an arch.
limit: A checked red slip says how this fragment was prepared. The lost side of the arch needs a separate source.
alt: Sloping tile fragment with sprays of flowers and a scalloped edge.
material: Fritware with red slip and underglaze design

title: Kashan mina’i beaker
fact: The museum identifies an overglaze design on this fritware beaker, classified as mina’i ware.
limit: The figures are a design on the object. Their names or occasions of use need an independent source.
alt: Tall translucent-looking beaker with small seated figures on two visible registers.
material: Fritware with overglaze design, mina’i ware

title: Jug with running animals
fact: The catalogue records a design in carved and underglaze-painted slip on this fritware jug.
limit: A silhouette alone cannot locate the cut and paint in the wall. The place attribution remains probable.
alt: A small blue-green jug with a running animal pattern and a short handle.
material: fritware with design in carved and underglaze-painted slip ("silhouette" ware)
dimensions: Overall: 13 x 14 cm (5 1/8 x 5 1/2 in.); Diameter of rim: 8.9 cm (3 1/2 in.)

title: Kashan lampas fragment
fact: The catalogue identifies this 25.5 by 15.6 cm surviving piece as lampas weave.
limit: The weave is known for the fragment. Its earlier full size and function remain open.
alt: A muted rectangular fragment densely patterned with floral repeats.

title: Damascus brass bowl
fact: The museum records sheet brass inlaid with silver and gold. Its description identifies twelve radiating arched panels.
limit: A viewing pattern may let someone count panels. It leaves the metal combination to the catalogue record.
alt: A low metal bowl with small interlacing patterns across its exterior.
material: sheet brass, inlaid with silver and gold

title: Mamluk quilted silk cap
fact: The cap is recorded as quilted silk lampas. Its production place is given as Syria or Egypt.
limit: The photograph does not establish a more precise workshop or the identity of a wearer.
alt: Low rounded cap with gold and dark panels meeting along stitched-looking lines.

title: Mamluk striped silk fragment
fact: The surviving textile includes silk and gold, in tabby and fancy weaves according to the museum.
limit: The recorded weave and stripe do not determine the earlier size of the cloth. Both possible places stay on the label.
alt: A fragment with red and gold stripes and several missing areas.
material: tabby and fancy weave; silk and gold

title: Tunisian bordered textile
fact: The catalogue lists linen, silk, metal and dye. It retains both garment and furnishing as possible object types.
limit: The border can be traced while the textile’s intended use stays open.
alt: Pale rectangle with a decorated band surrounding the whole edge.

title: Gujarat silk patolu sari
fact: The museum identifies silk double ikat and records the completed sari’s length as 419.1 cm.
limit: The two thread directions matter in double ikat. A painted pattern with the same edge would not establish that method.
alt: Long narrow silk sari with red borders and a dense geometric field.

title: Surat striped panel fragment
fact: The catalogue calls this silk striped fragment warp ikat in a tabby weave and dates it to 1900.
limit: One visible stripe can also be painted onto a surface. The thread direction belongs to the weave record.
alt: Small piece of red textile with straight closely spaced bands.

title: Bukhara munisak
fact: The museum identifies the woman’s garment as silk ikat velvet and dates it to 1850–75.
limit: A view of the motif cannot say whose robe it was. The fibre and weave belong to this catalogue item.
alt: A flared garment with wide sleeves and repeated red, gold and blue shapes.

title: Five-panel Bukhara pardah
fact: The record identifies five panels with silk warp and cotton weft and describes a printed lining separately.
limit: The pattern on the front does not establish the material or printing of the lining.
alt: A red-and-white hanging with zigzagged motifs and vertically divided bands.
material: warp ikat, warp-faced plain weave; silk warp; cotton weft; 5 panels./ lining: printed cotton, plain weave; 2 panels

title: Shahr-i Sabz khalat
fact: The museum describes this silk surcoat’s designs as cross-stitch embroidery.
limit: The garment’s pattern shows the design. Another record would be needed to name its wearer.
alt: Brightly embroidered coat with the sleeves spread and a patterned open front.

title: Khmer silk hanging or canopy
place: Khmer makers in Cambodia, in the museum’s attribution
fact: The record gives silk tabby weave with resist-dyed weft. It titles the piece as a wall hanging or ceiling canopy.
limit: A still view cannot determine whether the piece was hung flat or overhead on a particular occasion.
alt: A wide dark textile carries horizontal bands with pale elephants.

title: Sumba hinggi
fact: The catalogue lists cotton warp ikat for this hinggi and describes such mantles as made in pairs.
limit: This accession identifies this mantle. It does not identify a surviving mate.
alt: Dark-orange cloth with dense horizontal patterned bands and short fringe.

title: Mandaya dagmay
place: Mandaya makers in southeastern Mindanao, Philippines
fact: The museum describes a Mandaya dagmay woven from abacá. Its medium is listed as dyed plain-weave hemp.
limit: The cloth and its materials belong to the documented accession. Its pattern leaves an individual maker unnamed.
alt: A dark-brown fabric with repeated angular designs and a sectioned central field.

title: Teapot with Begonias
fact: The catalogue credits Seifū Yohei III and describes a design in underglaze blue with additional overglaze colours.
limit: A dark ornamental line can be redrawn. The original’s layers and maker rest on the collection record.
alt: Pale round teapot with a short spout and a spray of deep-blue leaves.
material: Porcelain with underglaze and overglaze colors
dimensions: height with lid: 7.5 cm (2 15/16 in.); width with handle: 10.5 cm (4 1/8 in.); Diameter: 9 cm (3 9/16 in.)

title: Sweets Bowl with Chrysanthemums
fact: The catalogue credits Seifū Yohei IV and records a moulded design alongside in-glaze and underglaze colour.
limit: A low-contrast view may hide the moulding. A painted outline alone cannot establish raised or recessed form.
alt: Low pale bowl with subtle flowers on the outside.
material: Porcelain with in-glaze and underglaze color and molded design
dimensions: height: 8.5 cm (3 3/8 in.); Diameter: 18.5 cm (7 5/16 in.)

title: Cloisonné napkin ring
collectionTitle: Napkin Ring with Cherry and Birds
fact: The catalogue identifies cloisonné enamel and a design with cherry and birds.
limit: A similar-looking coloured pattern does not establish the way its sections were made.
alt: Short blue enamel ring with flowers and small birds.

title: Qing bowl with splayed foot
fact: The museum describes metal outlines that divide colours in cloisonné enamel on this bowl.
limit: The coloured pattern and wire outlines are distinguishable evidence. The museum record leaves its owner unknown.
alt: A green enamel bowl with coloured motifs on a flared foot.
dimensions: Diameter: 10.5 cm (4 1/8 in.); Overall: 6.6 cm (2 5/8 in.)

title: Joseon buncheong fish bottle
collectionTitle: Bottle with Incised and Sgraffito Fish Design
fact: The museum classifies the bottle as buncheong stoneware with an incised fish design and sgraffito.
limit: A flat trace of the fish keeps the outline. It leaves the cut into the surface to another view or the catalogue.
alt: Pale narrow-necked bottle with a round belly and gently curving fish lines.
dimensions: Outer diameter: 17 cm (6 11/16 in.); Overall: 30.6 cm (12 1/16 in.)

title: Joseon peony and scroll bottle
collectionTitle: Bottle Inlaid with Peony and Scroll Design
fact: The catalogue distinguishes inlaid, incised and sgraffito work on this buncheong bottle.
limit: A peony outline can appear in more than one process. A closer surface or a study of the body is needed to distinguish them by sight.
alt: A green-grey narrow-necked bottle carries a large pale flower.
material: stoneware with inlaid, incised, and sgraffito design (Buncheong ware)
dimensions: Outer diameter: 17 cm (6 11/16 in.); Overall: 27 cm (10 5/8 in.)

title: Byzantine deep plate
collectionTitle: Deep Plate with Hawk and Foliage
fact: The museum lists sgraffito earthenware and titles the figure a hawk amid foliage.
limit: The named animal design does not date the moment the object was used or identify who used it.
alt: A deep round plate with a faint central bird and a darker edge.

title: Crescent gold earring
fact: The catalogue identifies gold filigree and cloisonné enamel and tentatively gives Constantinople.
limit: The photographed curve shows the design. Its precise workshop and the identity of a wearer remain open.
alt: A large gold wire loop meets a decorated crescent.

title: Portrait plate from Faenza
collectionTitle: Plate with a Portrait of a Gentleman
fact: The museum records tin-glazed earthenware and describes the central image as a portrait of a gentleman.
limit: A portrait and its painted setting do not give this person’s name.
alt: A blue plate with a portrait in the centre and a patterned ring.

title: Samadet faience plate
fact: The museum identifies faience, dates the plate to about 1770 and gives Samadet.
limit: The decorated surface and shaped lip are separate features. The illustration leaves the individual maker unknown.
alt: A decorated plate with a scalloped rim and a multicoloured central scene.

title: Sceaux Plate of Walnuts
fact: The museum records this object as faience and gives an overall height of 5.8 cm.
limit: The recognisable walnuts are represented on a ceramic object. A line drawing cannot establish their relief height.
alt: A plate with several walnut-shaped forms among painted flowers.

title: Mennecy underglaze cup
feature: blue line along the cup rim
fact: The museum credits the Mennecy–Villeroy Factory and records underglaze blue on soft-paste porcelain.
limit: A blue ornament alone is insufficient to identify a factory. Keep the attribution with its own record.
alt: A white fluted cup has a blue rim band and line around the foot.
material: soft-paste porcelain with underglaze blue decoration

title: Visigothic belt buckle
fact: The catalogue records bronze, garnets, glass, mother-of-pearl and gold foil.
limit: One coloured cell can resemble another in a small image. The material list belongs to the accession.
alt: A bronze buckle plate holds a red-and-green grid next to two clasps.
material: bronze with garnets, glass, mother of pearl, gold foil, traces of gilding; bronze and glass

title: Enamelled sugar tongs
place: St. Petersburg, Russia, in the museum’s attribution
fact: The museum names the House of Fabergé and workmaster Feodor Ivanovich Rückert and lists silver gilt with opaque cloisonné enamel.
limit: The collection’s attribution and metal record cannot be recovered from the handle colour alone.
alt: Small gold-coloured tongs with a narrow dark and colourful handle.

title: Cloisonné-mounted belt
fact: The catalogue lists enamel on copper, gilt metal mounts and cloisonné medallions.
limit: The belt brings several materials and linked parts into one whole. The overall length is for the whole belt.
alt: A long fine belt with regularly placed small decorated medallions.
material: enamel on copper with gilt metal mounts and cloisonné medallions

title: Roman millefiori glass bowl
fact: The museum describes a bowl made by joining patterned pieces of glass in a two-part mold.
limit: A surface picture preserves round marks. Another view is needed to show whether the pieces of a model continue through its body.
alt: A glass bowl carries many small multicoloured circles over its exterior.
dimensions: Overall: 3.8 x 8.8 cm (1 1/2 x 3 7/16 in.); Diameter of foot: 4 cm (1 9/16 in.)
